title: OmniVia Core Application Contract v1 - asynchronous job foundations
description: Job identity, state, progress, attempt, event, handle, and terminal-result shapes for asynchronous work started by an operation. This document declares no root type; it is a definition container only.

JobState.title: JobState
JobState.description: Open, dot-namespaced code naming where a job stands in its lifecycle, such as `queued` or `running` or `succeeded` or `failed` or `cancelled`. Open by design so a compatible minor release can add states without breaking existing decoders.

JobIdentity.title: JobIdentity
JobIdentity.description: The identity of one asynchronous job: what it is, which application operation started it, its immutable audit linkage, and, when applicable, which workspace it runs against.

job_id.description: Opaque, server-issued identifier of this job.

job_kind.description: Open code naming the kind of work this job performs, such as `ingestion.import`.

originating_operation.description: The application operation whose invocation started this job.

audit_reference.description: Immutable reference to the audit record for the operation invocation that started this job.

workspace_id.description: Workspace this job runs against, when the job is workspace-scoped.

JobProgressUnit.title: JobProgressUnit
JobProgressUnit.description: Open, dot-namespaced code naming what `JobProgress.completed_units`/`total_units` count, such as `item` or `byte` or `document`. Open by design so a compatible minor release can add units without breaking existing decoders.

JobProgress.title: JobProgress
JobProgress.description: A point-in-time progress statement for a running job.

unit.description: What `completed_units`/`total_units` count, so the counters are interpretable without job-kind-specific knowledge.

completed_units.description: Units of work completed so far, counted in `unit`.

total_units.description: Total units of work expected, when known in advance, counted in `unit`.

message.description: Human-readable progress note. Not a stable interface.

JobCancellationDisposition.title: JobCancellationDisposition
JobCancellationDisposition.description: Open, dot-namespaced code naming whether a job may be cancelled and where a requested cancellation stands, such as `not_cancellable` or `cancellable` or `cancellation_requested` or `cancelled`. Open by design; carries no scheduler, worker, lease, or persistence detail.

JobRetryDisposition.title: JobRetryDisposition
JobRetryDisposition.description: Open, dot-namespaced code naming whether a job may be retried and where a requested retry stands, such as `not_retryable` or `retryable` or `retry_scheduled`. Open by design; carries no scheduler, worker, lease, or persistence detail.

JobResumeDisposition.title: JobResumeDisposition
JobResumeDisposition.description: Open, dot-namespaced code naming whether a suspended or cancelled job may be resumed, such as `not_resumable` or `resumable` or `resume_requested`. Open by design; carries no scheduler, worker, lease, or persistence detail.

JobControl.title: JobControl
JobControl.description: The control actions a caller may take on a job: cancellation, retry, and resume. Deliberately exposes only these caller-facing dispositions, never scheduler, worker, lease, or persistence detail.

cancellation.description: Whether this job may be cancelled and where a requested cancellation stands.

retry.description: Whether this job may be retried and where a requested retry stands.

resume.description: Whether this job may be resumed and where a requested resume stands.

JobAttempt.title: JobAttempt
JobAttempt.description: One execution attempt of a job. A job that is retried has more than one attempt.

finished_at.description: When this attempt finished, when it has.

error.description: The failure this attempt ended with, when it failed.

JobEvent.title: JobEvent
JobEvent.description: One entry in a job's ordered event stream.

sequence.description: Monotonically increasing ordinal of this event within the job.

state.description: State the job was in when this event was recorded.

message.description: Human-readable event note. Not a stable interface.

JobHandle.title: JobHandle
JobHandle.description: What a caller holds to track a job over time: its identity, current state, latest known progress and attempt, and which control actions are available.

updated_at.description: When this job's state was last observed to change.

control.description: Which control actions a caller may take on this job right now.

JobCancellationOutcome.title: JobCancellationOutcome
JobCancellationOutcome.description: The explicit outcome recorded when a job's terminal state is cancellation, distinguishing it from an ordinary success or failure.

reason.description: Open code naming why the job was cancelled, such as `caller_requested` or `deadline_exceeded`.

JobTerminalSuccess.title: JobTerminalSuccess
JobTerminalSuccess.description: The final outcome of a job that succeeded. Carries `result` and never `error` or `cancellation`.

state.description: Terminal state the job reached, such as `succeeded`.

finished_at.description: When the job reached its terminal state.

attempts.description: Every execution attempt this job made, in order.

JobTerminalFailure.title: JobTerminalFailure
JobTerminalFailure.description: The final outcome of a job that failed. Carries `error` and never `result` or `cancellation`.

state.description: Terminal state the job reached, such as `failed`.

finished_at.description: When the job reached its terminal state.

attempts.description: Every execution attempt this job made, in order.

JobTerminalCancellation.title: JobTerminalCancellation
JobTerminalCancellation.description: The final outcome of a job that was cancelled. Carries `cancellation` and never `result` or `error`.

state.description: Terminal state the job reached, such as `cancelled`.

finished_at.description: When the job reached its terminal state.

attempts.description: Every execution attempt this job made, in order.

JobTerminalResult.title: JobTerminalResult
JobTerminalResult.description: The final outcome of a job once it has reached a terminal state, with the complete attempt history that led there. Exactly one of a success, a failure, or a cancellation, never a mix: each branch closes its property set and carries a unique required discriminator (`result`, `error`, or `cancellation`), so a payload combining or omitting all three matches no branch.
